units: Yalk. Ps. 672 נוטלין … ופורעין בפ׳ they borrow from one another in trust (without witnesses or note) and pay in trust; Midr. Till. to Ps. XIX בפינוסין, ed. Bub. בפטסין (corr. acc.).—Esp. שטר פ׳ a deed of trust, an instrument by which property is conveyed to a person in trust (fideicommissum) to use it in a certain way; a feigned sale or donation (for the purpose of eluding creditors &c.).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 2:2:1">Y. Keth. II, 26ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>נאמנין … ושטר פ׳ הוא</he> (not <cite ref="Q00291"><he>פוסיטים</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q00759"><he>פיסיטים</he></cite>) witnesses (signed on an instrument) are credited when they say, it was a deed of trust (v. <cite ref="A02041"><he>אֲמָנָה</he></cite>), or it was a feigned transfer.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 2:2:1">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Job 11:14">Job XI, 14</cite>) ‘if there be wrong in thy house, remove it’, this means a deed &c.; Bab.

<cite ref="Ketubot 19b:2">Keth. 19ᵇ</cite> <he>פסים</he>, (read with Ar. <cite ref="Q01300"><he>פָּסִיס</he></cite> q. v.). Ib. 79ᵃ <he>הרוצה … כותבת שטר פסים לאחרים</he> if a woman desires to withhold her property from her husband’s control, she may write out a deed of trust (a feigned transfer) to a third person (prior to her marriage); Tosef. ib. IX, 2 <he>כותבן שטר פטים לאחר</he> ed. Zuck. (Var. <he>בטפיח</he>, <he>כותבתן בטפוס</he>, corr. acc.).

<cite ref="Bava Batra 154b:6">B. Bath. 154ᵇ</cite> <he>אם אמר שטר פסים הוא זה</he> (Ms. H. <he>פיס</he>) if he says, it was a feigned sale (you persuaded me to a nominal sale in order to make people believe that you are a man of means).
